channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Almaty to Ban Coal Sales by 2027 as Part of Low-Emission Zone
item.description: Almaty plans to prohibit coal sales starting January 1, 2027, as part of its low-emission zone initiative. Coal deliveries to city depots will cease by the end of 2026. This measure aims to reduce air pollution, with ongoing efforts to transition businesses and homes from solid fuel to gas.

item.title: 288 Families Relocate from Turkistan Region to Labor-Shortage Areas in Kazakhstan
item.description: This year, 288 families, totaling 1,322 people, voluntarily migrated from the Turkistan region to northern and central Kazakhstan's labor-shortage areas. This represents 22% of the annual national quota. Migrants receive employment, housing, and social support under a state program.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Elkart and Mastercard Partner for Co-Badged Payment Card
item.description: The national payment system Elkart and Mastercard have signed a memorandum to develop joint digital payment projects, including a co-badged Elkart-Mastercard card. This new card will use Elkart's infrastructure domestically and Mastercard's international network abroad, allowing seamless transactions using existing Elkart funds.

item.title: Afghanistan and Russia Discuss Expanding Economic Ties and Investment
item.description: Afghan Prime Minister Mohammad Hassan Akhund met with Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk in Kabul to enhance bilateral relations and economic cooperation. Akhund highlighted Afghanistan's stability for investment, thanking Moscow for recognition. Overchuk expressed Russia's interest in investing in various Afghan sectors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Hungary Discuss Strengthening Strategic Partnership
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador Erlan Abdyldaev met with Hungarian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Anita Orbán in Budapest. The meeting focused on key areas of strategic partnership, trade, economy, investment, and humanitarian cooperation. Both sides noted the high level of interaction and the importance of further strengthening bilateral ties.

item.title: Asein Isaev Appointed Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Belgium
item.description: Asein Isaev has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Belgium. The decree was signed by President Sadyr Japarov. Isaev previously served as Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to France and Belgium from 2015 to 2020. He replaces Aydit Erkin, who was released from his post on November 9.

item.title: Asein Isaev Appointed Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Belgium
item.description: Asein Isaev has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Belgium. The relevant decree was signed by President Sadyr Japarov. This appointment marks a diplomatic shift for Kyrgyzstan in its relations with Belgium.

item.title: Air Astana to Launch Direct Flights from Almaty and Astana to Sharm El Sheikh
item.description: Air Astana will commence regular flights from Almaty on December 10 and from Astana on December 11 to Sharm El Sheikh, Egypt. Previously, this route was served only by charter flights. The airline stated that regular flight status will allow passengers to book tickets directly through its official channels. Flights from Almaty will operate twice weekly, and from Astana, also twice weekly.

item.title: Former Wife of Kuandyk Bishimbayev Explains Why She Didn't Warn Saltanat
item.description: Nazym Kaharman, the former wife of Kuandyk Bishimbayev, stated she did not warn Saltanat about his difficult character because she considered it inappropriate to speak ill of her ex-husband to his new partner. Kaharman mentioned she had warned Saltanat's sister three times about Bishimbayev's behavior, but it's unclear if Saltanat received these warnings. She described Bishimbayev as someone who perceives kindness as weakness.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Ukraine Dismissed from Post
item.description: Idris Kadyrkulov has been dismissed from his position as Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Ukraine. He also held concurrent ambassadorial roles in Moldova, Bulgaria, and Romania. The relevant decree was signed by President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Almaty Reduces Coal Usage, Aims for Gas Transition by 2026
item.description: Almaty is significantly reducing coal consumption, with 99.6% of private sector homes already connected to natural gas. The city plans to cease coal deliveries by rail to urban depots by the end of 2026 and encourage businesses to switch to gas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Receives 295 Convicted Citizens from Russia in 2026
item.description: In 2026, 295 convicted citizens were transferred from Russia to Kyrgyzstan for further imprisonment. The Prosecutor General's Office reported a significant increase in such transfers in recent years, with 237 individuals returned in 2025 alone. Procedures for another 65 are complete, awaiting transfer.

item.title: Kyrgyz Rights Activist Denied Documents from Detention Center Due to Destruction
item.description: Human rights activist Perizat Suranova was denied documents from Detention Center No. 21, which she needs for a compensation claim. The center stated that records of items she received during her detention from October 2022 to February 2023 were destroyed due to expired retention periods.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Clarifies Rules on Accessing Personal Data Without Consent
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development and Artificial Intelligence has clarified regulations regarding access to citizens' personal data. Certain government bodies, including police and courts, can access data without consent under specific legal provisions, such as for law enforcement or judicial proceedings. Access is limited to what is necessary for official functions.

item.title: Kazakh Company Solidcore Resources to Explore Precious Metals in Tajikistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Solidcore Resources has signed a five-year memorandum with Tajikistan's Main Directorate of Geology to expand geological exploration for precious and polymetallic ores. The agreement includes data exchange, joint research, and training for Tajik specialists. If exploration proves commercially viable, it could lead to new mining enterprises.

item.title: Woman Candidate Emerges in Kyrgyzstan's Presidential Race
item.description: Former Constitutional Chamber judge Klara Sooronkulova has submitted documents to run for president in Kyrgyzstan, becoming the sole female contender among 11 applicants. She registered via self-nomination on November 12. Candidates must gather 30,000 signatures by December 7 for registration, finalized on December 23. The election is set for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Notifying Passengers of Airfare Price Changes
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering implementing a system to notify passengers about changes in air ticket prices. The Ministry of Trade and Integration discussed this initiative, along with the possibility of a price calendar for flights. The Public Council also recommended that regulatory bodies investigate the transparency of domestic flight pricing and fare structures.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Cooperate with China Primarily at Government Level
item.description: Experts discussed the autonomy of Central Asian countries in their interactions with China. The focus was on who can influence Beijing's decisions in the region, rather than China's actions. While some believe effective agreements are possible, others doubt civil society's systematic influence.

item.title: Kazakhstan Improves Exchange Rate Forecast for Tenge Through 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bureau of Economic Research has revised its exchange rate forecast, expecting a stronger tenge by the end of 2026. The average dollar exchange rate is projected between 441 and 476 tenge in November and slightly weaker in December, reflecting recent currency strength.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Permanent Population Exceeds Current Statistics by 2.1 Percent
item.description: Uzbekistan's permanent population reached 39,047,321 as of January 15, 2026, according to final census results. This figure is 2.1% higher than current estimates, attributed to adjustments based on birth, death, and migration data. Males constitute 50.6% of the population.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Study Air Ticket Costs and Tariff Formation Mechanisms
item.description: Kazakhstan's Public Council under the Ministry of Trade has raised concerns about the transparency of air ticket prices. The council discussed the development of e-commerce, a regional digital services market, and pricing transparency for domestic air travel. The Ministry of Trade emphasized the importance of fair competition and consumer protection.

item.title: Unemployment Rate for Kazakhs Over 55 Reaches 8.6%
item.description: In the third quarter of 2026, Kazakhstan's unemployment rate for citizens aged 55-64 reached 8.6%, double the national average of 4.5%. This age group accounted for 96,700 job seekers. Women in this age bracket faced higher unemployment at 9.3% compared to men's 8%.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allow Trading of Foreign Stocks Through Local Brokers
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved regulations allowing the trading of foreign securities through local brokers and electronic platforms. The new rules, effective November 12, permit access to foreign stock exchanges. Specific requirements are set for investors, financial instruments, brokers, and settlements. Foreign securities must obtain approval from the National Agency for Projects Management.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Reviews Development in Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov visited the Issyk-Kul region and Balykchy to review socio-economic development from 2021-2026. Funding for the Issyk-Kul district increased over 12-fold, with industrial output six times higher than in 2021. New infrastructure, including schools and roads, was built, and 2,154 jobs were created.

item.title: Almaty to halt coal deliveries to city bases by year-end
item.description: Almaty plans to stop rail coal deliveries to city bases by the end of the year as part of a directive to relocate coal depots to the Almaty region. Lease agreements for current coal sites will also be terminated.

item.title: Kazakhstan aims to curb shadow economy, reducing its share to 15.7%
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing measures to combat its shadow economy, which accounted for 15.7% of GDP last year, an estimated 25 trillion tenge. The share has decreased by 12 percentage points over the past decade, reaching a historic low.

item.title: Commodity Market Overview: Gold and Silver Rise, Oil Declines
item.description: On November 13, the global commodity market saw mixed trends. While precious and industrial metals increased in value daily, their monthly performance remained low. Oil prices traded below $100 per barrel, and uranium's monthly growth slowed.

item.title: UK Imposes Sanctions on Russian Company Sibur with Kazakh Project Stakes
item.description: The United Kingdom has updated its sanctions list, including the Russian holding company Sibur, which has stakes in two projects in Kazakhstan. The company supports Russia's energy sector. This action adds to existing international measures against Russian entities.

item.title: Over One Thousand Educational Grants Awarded to Soldiers in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has distributed over a thousand educational grants to soldiers. A total of 8,823 servicemen participated in the competitive selection for these grants, which will allow them to pursue higher education after completing their military service.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree on New Round of Talks and Prisoner Exchange, No Territorial Breakthrough
item.description: Russian and US officials held substantive talks in the Kremlin. They agreed to continue negotiations and support a large-scale prisoner exchange. While progress was made on humanitarian issues, no breakthroughs were achieved regarding territorial disputes. Russia also reiterated its security concerns.

item.title: Over 1,000 Education Grants Allocated for Kazakh Conscripts
item.description: Kazakhstan has allocated over 1,000 education grants for conscripted soldiers to pursue higher education starting in autumn 2025. The interdepartmental commission approved 1,040 places, including 800 state grants and 240 within military higher education institutions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Increase Untaxed Income Threshold by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to increase the amount of income exempt from personal income tax starting January 1, 2027. The basic tax deduction may rise from 129,750 to 140,790 tenge per month, potentially increasing take-home pay for employees.

item.title: Uzbekistan's healthcare spending exceeds 17 trillion soms in nine months
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Uzbekistan's healthcare services reached 17.6 trillion soms, with Tashkent accounting for nearly half at 8 trillion soms. This represents a 14.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Hospital services constituted 32.3% of the total volume.

item.title: Kazakhstan allocates 5 billion tenge for domestic cancer drug development amid audit concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan has allocated 5 billion tenge for the development of a domestic cancer drug. However, the Supreme Audit Chamber found insufficient evidence of production readiness. Concerns were raised about payment procedures and the early release of funds to research organizations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry maintains low liquefied gas price despite below-cost levels
item.description: For the third time, Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has kept the price of liquefied petroleum gas unchanged, even though it is below the cost of production. This decision impacts the energy market and producers within the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Batken Province Reminds Coal Sellers of Price Limits
item.description: Specialists from the State Antimonopoly Agency in Batken, Kyrgyzstan, monitored coal sales points on November 12, reminding sellers of maximum retail prices. Set by order №21 on November 2, these limits, valid until January 18, 2027, cap the price of Suluktu coal at 10,000 soms per ton and local coal at 8,000 soms. Temporary state regulation of coal prices is in effect nationwide until January 18, 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan Customs Committee Responds to Criticism Over Phone Import Duties
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Customs Committee addressed journalist concerns regarding the impact of import duties on mobile phone prices. A committee spokesperson clarified the distinction between customs duties and IMEI registration fees. Officials argued that removing import duties on all goods would be illogical, emphasizing that businesses pass costs to consumers.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allow Foreign Stock Deals Only for Qualified Investors
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Agency for Advanced Projects has approved rules for trading foreign securities within a regulatory sandbox. The regulations, effective November 11, permit only qualified investors to engage in transactions involving foreign stocks, bonds, ETFs, and other listed assets. Trading will occur on the Tashkent Stock Exchange or via licensed investment intermediaries.

item.title: Poachers Injure Ecopolice Officer in Bukhara Region During Illegal Hunting
item.description: In the Bukhara region's Peshku district, an ecopolice officer was injured while confronting poachers engaged in illegal hunting with prohibited equipment. Five individuals were apprehended for hunting 13 rabbits in a protected area. An investigation is underway by the prosecutor's office.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis Claim Drone Attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West Oil Pipeline
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels announced a drone attack targeting the seventh pumping station of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two drones over Riyadh. The pipeline is crucial for transferring oil to the Red Sea, especially amid tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.
